title: Discrete series of U(p,q)
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Kernels kill bounded radical-invariant functions; dilations along isotropic subspaces
modules.note:
The file proves that, under hypotheses stated below, integration against an idempotent kernel kills
bounded continuous functions that are left invariant under a radical, namely the elements `r` with
`(r, 1) ∈ D` for a subgroup `D` of `G × ℂˣ`
(`New.DiscreteSeries.integral_idempotentKernel_mul_eq_zero`). It also proves that, for unitary
groups, dilations along an isotropic subspace meet every conjugate of a neighbourhood of `1`
(`New.DiscreteSeries.exists_conj_mem_dilationGroup`). The second result is used for the hypothesis
`hD_near` of the first.

The imported notions used in the statements are:
* `IsIdempotentKernel e`: `e` is continuous, integrable and self-adjoint, `e 1 ≠ 0`, and the
  convolution `e * δ_x * e` is `(e x⁻¹ / e 1) • e`;
* `U J`: the group of invertible matrices `g` with `gᴴ * J * g = J`;
* `dilationGroup A`: the pairs `(g, c)` with `g ∈ U J` and `c` a unit, such that `g * A = c • A`
  and `wᴴ * J * g * v = wᴴ * J * v` whenever the columns of `v` and `w` are `J`-orthogonal to
  those of `A`.
modules.literature:
Known result: coefficients of integrable discrete series are cusp forms. The vanishing of constant
terms is proved for any continuous self-adjoint integrable minimal idempotent `e` with `‖e‖ * ℓ`
integrable, tested on bounded continuous functions invariant under the radical, under the
hypotheses on `H`, `ℓ` and `D` stated below. Source: R. Godement, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 225
(1947) 521-523, 657-659; N. Wallach, Real Reductive Groups I (1988), ch. 7; the closest to the proof
here are B. Barnes, Proc. Edinburgh Math. Soc. 23 (1980), and A. Valette, Math. Ann. 294 (1992)
277-287.

modules.title: The real unitary group G₁, unipotent coordinates and Bessel functions
modules.group: Bessel models of the real unitary group
modules.note:
The form `(𝔰.middleGram N).splitGram` on the space Y₀ of column vectors indexed by `𝔰.BesselIndex`
is the sum of ϱ hyperbolic planes, the identity form on X₀ = A^κ and a line of norm −N. Its
archimedean version is the complex form `New.Shape.J₁`, whose space has basis `e_a`, `x_i`, `z`,
`e*_a` with `h(z, z) = -1` for the hermitian form `h`, and frame `e_0, …, e_{ϱ-1}, z`. The file
embeds the unitary group of X₀ in U(Y₀) and in `G₁`. It gives explicit elements of the unipotent
groups 𝖴⁰ = `New.Shape.Form.besselU0` and 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, and measures on them. It
then defines Bessel functions on `G₁`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_besselU_mul_toBesselH`: for N a unit, a coefficient ring with an element of trace one
  and an invertible hermitian form, every element of `besselS` is a product `u h` with `u` in
  `besselU` and `h` in the image of `New.toBesselH`.
* `New.Shape.G₁`, `New.Shape.J₁`: the group and its form.
* `New.RealPlace.unipotentOf`, `New.RealPlace.mem_besselU0_iff_unipotentOf`: a parametrization of
  the unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU0` that fixes the frame.
* `New.RealPlace.embedH`: the unitary group of the `x_i` inside `G₁`.
* `New.Shape.besselHaar₀`, `New.Shape.besselHaar`: measures on 𝖴⁰ and 𝖴, pushed forward from
  Lebesgue measure on the parameters and, for 𝖴, from its product with the measure on 𝖴⁰.
* `New.IsBesselFunction`: bounded measurable functions that transform by a character under the
  unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU` and by `rep` under `U(κ)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram T`: the Gram matrix of ϱ hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix T. Identity blocks pair the first and last ϱ indices, T is the middle block, and all other
  entries are zero.
* `New.inclMatrix`: for a map u : m → n of index sets, the n×m matrix whose j-th column is the
  standard basis vector e_{u(j)}.
* `New.frameMatrix`: the square submatrix on the rows and columns of the frame.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselS`: the Bessel subgroup, generated by the unipotent group 𝖴 =
  `New.Shape.Form.besselU` and the fixer H = `New.Shape.Form.besselH` of the basis vectors that
  are not indexed by κ.
modules.literature:
Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.FloorGroups`, `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bessel.UnipotentHaarMeasure`
and `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.ComplexPlace` for sources.

modules.title: Traces and L² bounds for Bessel functions
modules.group: Bessel models of the real unitary group
modules.note:
This file collects tools for estimating integrals of Bessel functions. It writes σ(u) + conj σ(u⁻¹),
for the sum σ(u) of simple root entries, as a trace against a fixed matrix. It proves abstract `L²`
bounds for convolutions on a unimodular group, and shows that norms of Bessel functions are
invariant under the Bessel subgroup `S = New.Shape.Form.besselS`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.besselCharMatrix`, `New.Filling.trace_besselCharMatrix_mul`: a fixed matrix C with
  tr(C u) = σ(u) + conj σ(u⁻¹) for every isometry u of the form `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`.
* `New.IsBoundedMeasurable.integral_inner_translate`: if `F * ψ = F` for an idempotent kernel `ψ`
  with `ψ 1 = d`, the inner products of the right translates of `F` are values of `ψ / d` times
  `‖F‖²`.
* `New.IsIdempotentKernel.enorm_integral_convolve_sq_le`: Schur's bound for a family of vectors of a
  Hilbert space with these inner products.
* `New.IsBoundedMeasurable.lintegral_sq_convolve_convolve_le`: the bound for `F * x` convolved once
  more with an integrable function.
* `New.IsBesselFunction.enorm_besselS_mul`: the norm of `W (s y)` equals that of `W y` for `s` in
  `S`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.convolve F x`: The function `y ↦ ∫ x a⁻¹ • F (y * a)`.
* `New.IsIdempotentKernel ψ`: `ψ` is continuous and integrable, `ψ g⁻¹ = conj (ψ g)`, `ψ 1 ≠ 0`,
  and `ψ * δ_t * ψ = (ψ t⁻¹ / ψ 1) ψ`.
* `New.orbitMeasure ρ volume`: A measure on `G` against which a left `S`-invariant function has the
  same integral as on `S \ G`.

modules.title: Haar measures on the Bessel unipotent groups 𝖴⁰ ⊆ 𝖴 and σ-finiteness on G₁
modules.group: Bessel models of the real unitary group
modules.note:
Let `𝔰` be a shape and let 𝖴⁰ ⊆ 𝖴 be the Bessel unipotent subgroups (`New.Shape.Form.besselU0`,
`New.Shape.Form.besselU`) of the unitary group `𝔰.G₁`, which is `(𝔰.middleGram 1).G` (so 𝖴⁰ is
`(𝔰.middleGram 1).besselU0`). The elements of 𝖴 are block upper unitriangular for the levels of the
basis indices, and 𝖴⁰ also fixes the frame e_0, …, e_{ϱ-1}, z. The measures `New.Shape.besselHaar₀`
on 𝖴⁰ and `New.Shape.besselHaar` on 𝖴 are images of Lebesgue measure under explicit
parametrisations.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.RealPlace.injective_freeEntries_besselU0`, `New.RealPlace.injective_freeEntries_besselU`: the
  free entries (`New.RealPlace.freeEntries`: the entries at the free positions in the rows e_a, plus
  the imaginary parts at (e_a, e*_a)) are injective on 𝖴⁰ and on 𝖴.
* `New.RealPlace.measurePreserving_freeEntries_besselHaar₀`,
  `New.RealPlace.measurePreserving_freeEntries_besselHaar`: the free entries carry these measures to
  Lebesgue measure.
* `New.RealPlace.isUnimodularHaar_besselHaar₀`: `New.Shape.besselHaar₀` is a two-sided Haar measure
  (`New.RealPlace.IsUnimodularHaar`). An instance gives the same for `New.Shape.besselHaar`.
* `New.RealPlace.eichlerVectors`, `New.RealPlace.eichlerScalars`: the matrices ω and μ that describe
  an element of 𝖴⁰ as an Eichler map with matrix entries (`New.RealPlace.eichlerMatrix`).
* `New.RealPlace.homogeneousBall`: the balls ‖ω‖ ≤ ρ, ‖μ‖ ≤ ρ² in 𝖴⁰. Radii add under multiplication
  (`New.RealPlace.mul_mem_homogeneousBall`), and the volume is proportional to a power of the radius
  (`New.RealPlace.besselHaar₀_homogeneousBall`).
* `New.RealPlace.exists_tube`: there is a compact set whose slices along 𝖴⁰ have controlled measure
  (`New.RealPlace.IsTube`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.G₁`: The unitary group of the complex hermitian form made of ϱ hyperbolic planes, the
  standard positive form on κ, and one vector z with h(z, z) = −1.
* `New.Shape.BesselIndex`: The index set of the basis e_a; x_i (i in κ), z; e*_a, where a runs over
  `Fin ϱ`. The level is a at e_a, ϱ on the middle block and 2ϱ − a at e*_a (a counted from 0).
modules.literature:
No Bessel model is constructed here. This file gives coordinates and Lebesgue–Haar measure on the
unipotent radical and on its subgroup fixing the frame, balls and tubes for the latter, and the
σ-finiteness of Haar measures on the ambient unitary group. Source for the setting: H. Xue, Bessel
models for real unitary groups: the tempered case, Duke Math. J. 172 (2023) 995-1031; R.
Beuzart-Plessis, Astérisque 418 (2020).

modules.title: Haar measure of G₁ and the fibre measure on frames
modules.group: Bessel models of the real unitary group
modules.note:
The group `New.Shape.G₁` is the unitary group of the form `New.Shape.J₁`, of rank `r`, with basis
`e_a`, `x_i`, `z`, `e*_a`: there are `ϱ` hyperbolic pairs `e_a, e*_a`, the span `X₀` of the `x_i` is
positive definite of rank `k`, and `z` is negative. The frame is `e_0, …, e_{ϱ-1}, z`, and 𝖴⁰ is the
unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU0` that fixes it. The file compares Haar measure of G₁ with
the fibre measure of the Gram map on tuples of vectors.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LeGramFibre J E m` says that the image of `m` under `g ↦ g E` is at most the fibre measure of
  the Gram map `E' ↦ E'ᴴ J E'` over the Gram matrix of `E`.
* `New.LeFibreMeasure μ ν π b l` says that `l` is at most the fibre measure `dμ / dν` of `π` over
  `b`.
* `New.volU j` is `vol U(j)`; the measure `volume` on G₁ is Haar measure, normalised through the
  compact dual, and on the unitary group H = U(X₀) it is the Haar measure of mass one.

Main results:
* `New.LeGramFibre.mconv_embedH_le`: tuples with the Gram matrix of the basis vectors outside `X₀`.
  These vectors have fixer `H = U(X₀)`; if their image under `m` is below the fibre measure, then
  `m ∗ dh` is at most `vol U(r) / (2 ^ (r - k) vol U(k))` times Haar measure of G₁.
* `New.RealPlace.lintegral_eq_unipotent_coords`: Lebesgue measure on the `ϱ`-tuples dual to
  `e_0, …, e_{ϱ-1}` and orthogonal to `z`, in coordinates given by 𝖴⁰ and the Gram matrix.
* `New.LeGramFibre.mconv_fixerHaar_le`: frames. The standard frame has fixer 𝖴⁰ H, with the measure
  `ds = New.RealPlace.fixerHaar`; if the image of the frame under `m` is below the fibre measure,
  then `m ∗ ds` is at most `vol U(r) / (2 ^ (ϱ + 1) vol U(k))` times Haar measure of G₁.
modules.literature:
Known result: the fibre measure of the Gram map on tuples of vectors, in terms of Haar measure of
the unitary group. The file proves the inequality that is used. Siegel, Über die analytische Theorie
der quadratischen Formen, Ann. of Math. 36 (1935).

modules.title: Floor groups, Weyl elements and the Bessel subgroup of a split unitary group
modules.group: Floors and Bruhat decomposition of unitary groups
modules.note:
We study the unitary group of the form `T.splitGram` over a commutative ring with involution. This
form has `𝔰.ϱ` hyperbolic planes and a middle block `T`. We define the floor groups `H_l`, `𝒩_l`,
`Q_l` and Weyl elements exchanging `e_a` and `e*_a`. These serve a descent through the hyperbolic
pairs, one pair at a time. We then study the Bessel subgroup `S` (`New.Shape.Form.besselS`),
generated by the block unitriangular isometries `𝖴` (`New.Shape.Form.besselU`) and the isometries
`H` (`New.Shape.Form.besselH`) that fix all basis vectors outside `κ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Shape.Form.floorGroup`: the fixer `H_l` of the floors below `l`. It decreases from `⊤` at
  `l = 0` to `⊥` for `l ≥ ϱ + 2`.
* `New.Shape.Form.unipotentBelow`, `New.Floors.FloorGroups.floorUnipotent`,
  `New.Shape.Form.partialUnitriangularGroup`: the groups `𝒩_{<l}`, `𝒩_l = H_l ∩ 𝒩_{<l+1}` and `Q_l`.
  The first increases to `New.Shape.Form.besselU` and the third decreases to it.
* `New.Floors.FloorGroups.leadingMinor_frameGram_partialUnitriangularGroup_mul`,
  `New.Filling.leadingMinor_frameGram_besselU_mul`: the leading minors of order at most `l` of the
  matrix of the products `h(f_a, γ f_b)` depend only on the double coset of `γ` under `Q_l`, and all
  of them only on the double coset under `𝖴`.
* `New.besselS_le_normalizer_besselU`: `S` normalises `𝖴`.
* `New.div_mem_unitaryLevel_of_besselU_mul`: the `h` in `H` with `h y` in `𝖴 K`, for a principal
  congruence subgroup `K`, lie in one right coset of `H ∩ K`.
* `New.simpleRootSum`, `New.simpleRootSum_mul`, `New.simpleRootSum_eq_zero_of_mem_besselH`: the sum
  of the entries just above the diagonal on the frame is additive on `S` and zero on `H`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: the Gram matrix `J` of ϱ hyperbolic planes and a middle space with
  Gram matrix `T`: identity blocks pair the first and last ϱ indices, `T` is the middle block, all
  else is zero. `T.G` is its unitary group.
* `New.Shape.BesselIndex`: the basis indices. `inl a` is `e_a`, `eStar a` = `inr (inr a)` is `e*_a`;
  the middle indices are those in `κ` and one more, `z`. `𝔰.n` is `ϱ + 1`.
* `New.BesselIndex.level`: `a` at `e_a`, `ϱ` on the middle block, `2ϱ - a` at `e*_a`.
* `New.Shape.besselFrame`: the frame `f = (e_0, …, e_{ϱ-1}, z)`; `𝔰.top` is the position of `z`.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`: the isometries that are block upper unitriangular for the levels.
modules.literature:
The file belongs to two known theories: isotropic flags in unitary groups (see
`Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.ComplexPlace`), and Poincaré series along a Bessel subgroup with their
unfolding, for which it supplies the groups. Sources: A. Borel, Introduction to automorphic forms,
Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 9 (1966) (Poincaré series); V. Platonov, A. Rapinchuk, Algebraic groups and
number theory (1994) §7.1; for the set-up, W. T. Gan, B. Gross, D. Prasad, Astérisque 346 (2012).

modules.title: Heisenberg elements, measures of the floors, hyperbolic bases and Plancherel at a place
modules.group: Floors and Bruhat decomposition of unitary groups
modules.note:
Algebra and measure theory on the unitary group `G` of the form `New.Shape.Form.splitGram T`, first
over a ring with involution and a `τ` of trace one, then over a place `A` (`New.Floors.Place`),
along its floors. The basis is `e_a`, a middle block, `e*_a` (`a < ϱ`). `V_l` is spanned by the
basis vectors of floor at least `l`: for `l ≤ ϱ`, the middle block and the pairs with `l ≤ a`. `h`
is the form. The frame `f_0, …, f_ϱ` (`New.Shape.besselFrame`) is `e_0, …, e_(ϱ-1)` followed by
the last vector `z` of the middle block.

In `New.Floors.FloorGroups`, the groups `floorGroup`, `unipotentBelow`, `floorUnipotent` and
`partialUnitriangularGroup` are `G_l = U(V_l)`, `N_(<l)`, `N_l = G_l ∩ N_(<l+1)` and `Q_l`. The
group `Q_l` consists of the elements unitriangular on the first `l` frame vectors, for `l ≤ ϱ + 1`.

`∗ₘ` is convolution of measures, so `μ ∗ₘ dirac s` is the right translate of `μ` by `s`.

* `New.Floors.TraceOne.heisenbergElem`, `New.Floors.FloorGroups.exists_eq_heisenbergElem_of_mem`:
  `N_a` is a Heisenberg group, given by Eichler maps.
* `New.Floors.FloorGroups.bijOn_mulVec_eStar`: `u ↦ u e*_a` maps `N_a` bijectively onto the
  isotropic vectors `y` of `V_a` with `h(e_a, y) = 1`.
* `New.Floors.FloorGroups.existsUnique_prod_of_mem_besselU`: an element of `N_(<ϱ)` is a product in
  `N_0 ⋯ N_(ϱ-1)` with unique factors.
* `New.Floors.Place.heisenbergMeasure`, `New.Floors.ascConv`: invariant measures on `N_l` and, by
  convolution, on `N_(<j)`.
* `New.Floors.HyperbolicBasis`, `New.Floors.HyperbolicBasis.floorQuadricMeasure`: hyperbolic bases
  of `V_ϱ` and `V_b`, and measures on quadrics in `V_b`, which disintegrate the Haar measure
  (`New.Floors.HyperbolicBasis.isDisintegration_floorVolume`).
* `New.Floors.Place.plancherel_inequality`: Plancherel's inequality on `A ^ ι`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.SplitIndex`: The index set made of ϱ indices, a middle set μ, and ϱ further indices, as a
  disjoint union.
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: The Gram matrix of ϱ hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix T: identity blocks pair the first and last ϱ indices, T is the middle block, all else is
  zero.
* `New.Floors.FloorGroups.floorOf`: The floor of a basis index: `a` for `e_a` and `e*_a`, `ϱ` for
  `z`, `ϱ + 1` for the other middle indices.
* `New.inclMatrix`: For a map u: m → n of index sets, the n×m matrix whose j-th column is the
  standard basis vector e_{u(j)}.

modules.title: Solving the equation of a quadric in a block of coordinates
modules.group: Floors and Bruhat decomposition of unitary groups
modules.note:
Let a hermitian form T on A^κ be the orthogonal sum of an orthonormal block and of its complement.
On a quadric in a hyperbolic plane plus T the part w of a vector outside the block is free, and the
part in the block lies on a quadric of the block, whose value is that of the given quadric minus
h(w, w). The measure of the quadric is the volume in w times the measures of these quadrics of the
block. This holds at any place, for any s-finite kernel that disintegrates the volume of the block
along its form.

## Main definitions and results
* `New.Floors.Place.IsSolvedIn`: a measure is the volume in the coordinates outside a block times
  an s-finite kernel of measures in the coordinates of the block, each of mass at most M on a box.
* `New.Floors.Place.IsDisintegration.lintegral_lintegral_comm`: on the orthogonal sum of two
  spaces, each with an s-finite kernel that disintegrates its measure, the equation of a quadric
  may be solved in either of them.
* `New.Floors.Place.IsDisintegration.isSolvedIn_quadricMeasure`: the measure of a quadric is solved
  in an orthonormal block, given an s-finite kernel on the quadrics of the block that disintegrates
  the volume and gives mass at most M to a box.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.Place`: a star ring A with Haar volume, an element τ of trace one, a skew unit δ and
  a Haar measure ν on the skew elements.
* `New.Floors.Place.quadricMeasure`: the measure on the quadric h(y, y) = δ⁻¹ b in a hyperbolic
  plane plus T, the image of a product measure under `New.Floors.Place.flatChart`. Here b, the
  index of the quadric, is skew.
* `New.Floors.Place.IsDisintegration`: a family of measures on the quadrics of a form, continuous
  in the index, whose integral over the index is a given measure.
modules.literature: Elementary: Tonelli's theorem and the invariance of Haar measure.

modules.title: The big cell: Bruhat decomposition of terms with non-zero leading minors, and its freeness
modules.group: Floors and Bruhat decomposition of unitary groups
modules.note:
The big cell of the Bruhat decomposition for the unipotent group `𝖴` = `New.Shape.Form.besselU`
(isometries that are block upper unitriangular in the basis below), over a ring with involution. The
existence of the decomposition is proved assuming an element `τ` with `τ + star τ = 1` (`TraceOne`).

* `New.Filling.exists_big_cell_decomp`: over a field with such a `τ`, if the leading minors
  `δ_1, …, δ_{n-1}` of `Z(γ)` are nonzero, then `γ ∈ 𝖴 w_p σ 𝖴` with `σ` fixing the hyperbolic
  pairs. Here `n = ϱ + 1`.
* `New.Filling.big_cell_factors_unique`: the element `u⁻¹ w_p σ u'` determines `p a` for `a < ϱ`,
  `σ`, `u` and `u'`. `New.Filling.big_cell_unique` is the case of one fixed `σ`.
* `New.Filling.exists_integral_big_cell_decomp`, `New.Filling.big_cell_factors_mem_intGL`: for a
  form that is unimodular over a subring `R` closed under `star` (`IsStarStable R`), the factors of
  an element of `GL(R)` whose leading minors are units of `R` lie in `GL(R)`.

`Z(γ)` = `New.Shape.Form.frameGram T γ` is the matrix of products of the frame
`(e_0, …, e_{ϱ-1}, z)` with its image, indexed by `Fin n`; its last index `𝔰.top` is the one of `z`.
`New.Floors.FloorGroups.weylElem j p` (`w_p`) sends `e_a` to `p a • e*_a` and `e*_a` to
`(star (p a))⁻¹ • e_a` on the first `j` hyperbolic pairs, and `New.Shape.Form.floorGroup j` is the
group of isometries that fix these pairs. The floor `j` is the `j`-th hyperbolic pair `(e_j, e*_j)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.BesselIndex`: The index set of the basis: `inl a` for e_a, `inr (inl _)` for the middle
  vectors, among them z, and `inr (inr a)` for e*_a.
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: The Gram matrix of ϱ hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix T: identity blocks pair the first and last ϱ indices, T is the middle block, all else is
  zero.
modules.literature:
This is a case of the known Bruhat decomposition of a unitary group on its big cell. See
`Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.ComplexPlace`.

modules.title: Fourier kernels between solved measures
modules.group: Floors and Bruhat decomposition of unitary groups
modules.note:
The measure theory, valid at any place, that bounds the kernel ψ(ξ ⟨v, y⟩), tested on measurable
integrable functions that vanish off a given set. The square norm of a function is the square of its
L² norm. A measure that is solved in a block has three kinds of coordinates: those of the block,
whose measures give bounded mass to a box; inner coordinates, in which Plancherel's inequality is
applied; and the remaining outer coordinates, which are estimated by the volume of a box.

* `New.Floors.Place.FourierSqNormLe`: the kernel ψ(ξ ⟨v, y⟩) multiplies square norms by at most a
  given constant. The bound passes to images of the measures.
* `New.Floors.Place.IsSolvedIn.setLIntegral_le`: a bound for the integral, over a box, of a function
  of the inner coordinates by its integral in those coordinates alone.
* `New.Floors.Place.IsSolvedIn.fourierSqNormLe`: the bound for the kernel between two measures that
  are solved in two disjoint blocks.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.Place`: a place A, with its character ψ, its modulus |·| = `modulus` and the constant
  c = `kernelBound` of Plancherel's inequality.
* `New.Floors.Place.IsSolvedIn`: a measure on A^κ is the volume in the coordinates off a block times
  a family of measures in the coordinates of the block, each of mass at most M on a box.
* `New.Floors.coordinateBox`: the box of a set R, that is, the vectors with all coordinates in R.
modules.literature: Standard consequences of Fubini's theorem and the inequalities of Cauchy–Schwarz and Plancherel.

modules.title: The place ℂ: polar coordinates, Cartan decomposition and the measure of the hyperboloid
modules.group: Floors and Bruhat decomposition of unitary groups
modules.note:
The archimedean instance of the local theory: the place `ℂ` and the top floor `ϱ` of the group
`New.Shape.G₁`, the unitary group of `ϱ` hyperbolic planes plus `V_ϱ = X₀ ⊕ ℂ z`, where `X₀ = ℂ^κ`
is standard and `h(z, z) = -1`. `New.RealPlace.embedH` embeds `U(X₀)` (written `U 1`) in it.
`floorGroup l` is the subgroup that fixes the basis vectors of the floors below `l`.

modules.title: Measures of a floor below fibre measures, at the place ℂ
modules.group: Floors and Bruhat decomposition of unitary groups
modules.note:
The group `New.Shape.G₁` is the unitary group of the complex form `h` (Gram matrix `𝔰.J₁`) with
basis `e_a`, `x_i` (`i : κ`), `z`, `e*_a`: `ϱ` hyperbolic pairs `e_a, e*_a`, the `x_i` orthonormal
and `h(z, z) = -1`. The pair of index `a` has floor `a`, `z` has floor `ϱ` and the `x_i` have floor
`ϱ + 1` (`New.Floors.FloorGroups.floorOf`); `V_b`, for a floor `b : Fin 𝔰.n` (so `b ≤ ϱ`), is
spanned by the basis vectors of floor at least `b`; `oppositeIndex` exchanges the indices of `e_a`
and `e*_a`.

A vector `y` is chosen with given products with earlier basis vectors and with a given norm
`h(y, y)`. Here `New.LeFibreMeasure μ ν π b l` says that the measure `l` is at most the fibre
measure `dμ / dν` of the map `π` over the point `b`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.leFibreMeasure_frameVector`: for the frame vector of a floor, half the quadric measure
  of the floor is at most the fibre measure.
* `New.Floors.leFibreMeasure_dualVector`: for the dual vector, half the measure of the Heisenberg
  group of the floor is at most the fibre measure.

The factor one half arises because these measures are quotients by `d(h(y, y) / 2)`. The last
section proves that the measures of the Heisenberg groups are invariant under inversion, as is the
Haar measure of the unitary group of the span of the `x_i`, carried into `G₁`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.HyperbolicBasis.floorQuadricMeasure`: The measure on a quadric in V_b: the image of
  `New.Floors.Place.quadricMeasure` with parameter β under the basis `F.floorBasis b`.
* `New.Floors.Place.heisenbergMeasure`: The measure on the Heisenberg group of floor `a`: the image
  of `dv` times the skew measure under the map that sends `(v, β)` to the isometry with
  `e*_a ↦ e*_a + v + (β - h(v, v) / 2) e_a`. For `a ≥ ϱ` it is the unit mass at `1`.
* `New.Shape.besselFrame`: The frame `(e_0, …, e_(ϱ-1), z)`, with one vector on each floor up to
  `ϱ`.
* `New.Floors.complexPlace`: The place `ℂ`: `τ = 1/2`, `δ = i/2`, `ν` the image of Lebesgue measure
  under `r ↦ r i`, modulus `‖x‖ ^ 2`, character `x ↦ exp (x - x̄)` and constant `c = π ^ 2`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.ComplexPlace` for sources.

modules.title: Laurent polynomials on the torus and Weyl's character and dimension formulas
modules.group: Characters and orbital integrals of discrete series
modules.note:
Let `ε : n → ℤˣ` be a family of signs and `K = New.maxCompactU ε` the group of unitary matrices in
the unitary group of `New.signMatrix ε`. Its Weyl group consists of the permutations `w` with
`ε ∘ w = ε`. Laurent polynomials are the elements of `ℂ[n → ℤ]`; they are evaluated on the diagonal
torus by `New.Orbital.torusEval`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.HCParam.rootProd l r`: the product `∏ (x_a - x_b)` over the pairs with `r (ε a) (ε b)` and
  `l b < l a`, where `r` is `Eq` for the compact roots and `Ne` for the noncompact roots.
  `New.Orbital.rootProd_mem_leadingMonomials` finds its top monomial, whose exponent
  `New.HCParam.lowerCount l r a` counts such `b`.
* `New.Orbital.alternant`, `New.Orbital.IsWeylAntisymm`: the alternants `∑ sgn(w) x ^ (μ ∘ w)` over
  the Weyl group, and functions of the exponent that are antisymmetric.
* `New.HCParam.kTypeChar`: the average over conjugation of the matrix coefficient
  `New.weightMinors ν` (a product of principal minors), divided by `New.HCParam.kTypeNormSq ν`.
* `New.Orbital.weyl_character_kTypeChar`, `New.Orbital.weyl_denominator`: Weyl's character and
  denominator formulas for `K`. The first joins
  `New.Orbital.exists_kTypeChar_diagTorusK_eq_torusEval` (the character is a Laurent polynomial) and
  `New.Orbital.torusEval_rootProd_mul_kTypeChar_eq_alternant` (the formula).
* `New.weyl_dimension_formula`: Weyl's dimension formula for `U(n)`.
* `New.Variety.trace_weylRep`: Weyl's character formula at a tuple `g` of invertible matrices with
  distinct eigenvalues, reduced to the diagonal case `New.weyl_character` by conjugation.

Notions from other files:
* `New.HCParam ε`: integer vectors `n → ℤ`, used as weights and as doubled parameters `l = 2λ`.
* `New.HCParam.lowestKType`: the integer vector `Λ = λ + ρ - 2ρ_c` for a parameter `l = 2λ`, the
  highest weight of the lowest `K`-type. With all signs `1` one has `ρ_c = ρ`.
* `New.weylRep κ e`: the representation of `∏_τ GL(n_τ)` sending `g` to `∏_τ det(g_τ) ^ e_τ` times
  the Schur matrix `New.schur κ g`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Weyl character formula for U(n) and products of unitary groups. Here the formula for
`K` is deduced from the one for Schur modules at diagonal matrices (`New.weyl_character`): by
Schur's lemma, normalised means over conjugation of products of principal minors are traces of
twisted Schur modules. The dimension formula is obtained by a limit at 1, and the formula for
`∏_τ GL_a(ℂ)` at elements with distinct eigenvalues by diagonalisation. Source: H. Weyl, The
Classical Groups (1939), ch. VII; Fulton and Harris, Representation Theory (1991), Lectures 24-25.

See also `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Character.FormalDegree`.

modules.title: K-type multiplicities of the discrete series and orbital integrals as Laurent polynomials
modules.group: Characters and orbital integrals of discrete series
modules.note:
Let `G = New.USign ε` be the unitary group of `diag ε`, and let `K = New.maxCompactU ε` be its
subgroup of unitary matrices. Let `ψ = New.HCParam.dsCoeff l` be the discrete series coefficient
with parameter `l = 2λ`. On the torus `New.diagTorus ε`, consider the normalised orbital integral
Θ(x) = `New.HCParam.formalDegree l` ∫_G ψ(g⁻¹ x g) dg. Θ times suitable products of differences
`x_a - x_b` is a Laurent polynomial, and the integrality of the multiplicities is the key input for
this.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Orbital.exists_kType_multiplicity`: for a dominant weight ν and a large gap,
  `formalDegree * ∫_G ∫_K conj (kTypeChar ν k) ψ(g⁻¹ k g)` is a natural number, `1` for ν equal to
  the lowest `K`-type `New.HCParam.lowestKType l` and `0` for ν off
  `lowestKType l + New.HCParam.rootCone l`.
* `New.Orbital.integrable_mul_dsCoeff_conj`: for the gap 500 n³ + 10 n⁵, the orbital integrals times
  a power of the product over the noncompact roots converge absolutely, uniformly on `K`.
* `New.Orbital.IsConeSeriesMultiple`: `P` is `D` times a formal series with coefficient `1` at
  `x^a` whose exponents lie in alternants of weights in `a` plus the root cone.
* `New.Orbital.exists_laurent_orbital_integral`: the orbital integral times the denominators is a
  Laurent polynomial that is such a multiple.

Notions from other files:
* `New.weightMinors`: the coefficient m_ν of a highest vector of weight ν, a product of principal
  minors and a power of the determinant.
* `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`: l = 2λ is a parameter with |λ_i - λ_j| ≥ 500 n³ + A whenever
  ε_i ≠ ε_j.
* `New.IsKDominant ε (-l) ν`, below "`K`-dominant in the order of `-l`": `ν j ≤ ν i` whenever
  `ε i = ε j` and `l j < l i`, so ν is dominant for the compact roots that are positive for l.
* `New.HCParam.lowestKType`: Λ = λ + ρ - 2ρ_c, the highest weight of the lowest K-type.
* `New.HCParam.formalDegree`: for signs ε and l = 2λ, the reciprocal of the integral of |c_λ|² over
  U(diag ε) for the compact dual measure.
modules.literature: See `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Character.FormalDegree`.

modules.title: Orbital integrals of discrete series coefficients and Weyl characters of U(n)
modules.group: Characters and orbital integrals of discrete series
modules.note:
This file begins the computation of the orbital integrals of the discrete series coefficient
`New.HCParam.dsCoeff l` of `G = U(diag ε)` over the compact torus. Here `l = 2λ` is the parameter,
and `ε` is implicit in its type. If `l` has a gap then, at a point `x` of the torus with
`diag ε * x` accretive (`A` accretive: `A + Aᴴ` positive definite), the orbital integral is, up to a
constant of modulus one, a multiple of Weyl's character of `U(n)` of highest weight `λ - ρ`, minus
an error given by an integral over the unitary matrices outside the open orbit `G B`. Here `B` is
the group of invertible matrices that are upper triangular for `l`, that is, `b i j = 0` whenever
`l j < l i`; they are lower triangular when the coordinates are listed with `λ` decreasing. If `o`
reverses the order of `l`, the error is small at `diag(t ^ o i)` for small `t = 2⁻¹ ^ s`, so a
Laurent polynomial that is a multiple of it has no monomial of low level.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.le_norm_weightMinors_twoPowDiagConj`: for unitary `u`, if `f` decreases along `l` by steps of
  at least `|m|` and `h ≤ |l i - l j|`, a lower bound for `New.weightMinors l` at `u* diag(2^f) u`
  by its value at `diag(2^f)` and the entry `u i j`.
* `New.Orbital.orbital_eq_char_sub_offOrbitIntegral`: the formula for the orbital integral described
  above, with the error `New.Orbital.offOrbitIntegral`.
* `New.Orbital.coeff_eq_zero_of_low_level`: if `l` has a gap and `o` reverses its order, a Laurent
  polynomial that is a multiple of this error has no monomial of low level, by the bound
  `New.Orbital.exists_norm_offOrbitIntegral_le`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: `l = 2λ` has distinct entries of the parity of `card n - 1`, and those of
  `λ` with different signs `ε` differ by at least `h`.
* `New.paramAddRho`: The integer vector `λ + ρ`, for ρ the half sum of the roots positive for `l`.
* `New.HCParam.dsCoeff`: The function c_λ on complex matrices given by Flensted-Jensen's integral
  `New.HCParam.flenstedJensen`; on K = U(diag ε) ∩ U(n) it is m_Λ with Λ = λ + ρ − 2ρ_c.
* `New.diagTorus`: For a tuple t of complex numbers of modulus one, the diagonal matrix diag(t) as
  an element of U(diag ε); `New.diagTorusK x` is diag(x) as an element of `maxCompactU 1`, which is
  U(n).
* `New.Orbital.torusEval`: For a tuple x of unit complex numbers, the algebra homomorphism from
  Laurent polynomials to ℂ sending the monomial of exponent ν to ∏ x_a^{ν_a}.
modules.literature:
This is part of the known computation of the discrete series character on the compact Cartan
subgroup by orbital integrals, see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Character.FormalDegree`.

modules.title: Harish-Chandra's formula for formal degrees and stable orbital integrals
modules.group: Characters and orbital integrals of discrete series
modules.note:
`New.Orbital.formalDegree_eq_weylDimensionPoly` is Harish-Chandra's formula for the formal degree of
a discrete series of `G = U(diag ε)`, and `New.Orbital.neg_one_pow_mul_sum_integral_dsKernel` gives
the stable sum of the orbital integrals of `New.HCParam.dsKernel` over the compact torus, both for a
parameter `l = 2λ` of gap `500 n³ + 10 n⁵`; `New.Orbital.harish_chandra_degree_and_orbital` states
the two together. By `New.Orbital.exists_laurent_orbital_integral` the orbital integral times a
product of roots is a Laurent polynomial; it is identified by comparing monomials of low level
(`New.Orbital.orbital_eq_char_sub_offOrbitIntegral`, `New.Orbital.coeff_eq_zero_of_low_level`).
The formal degree, with its constant, is read off from one coefficient in this comparison. The
orbital integrals converge absolutely by `New.Orbital.integrable_dsCoeff_conj`.

Conventions: `New.HCParam.rootProd l r` is the product of `x_a - x_b` over the pairs with
`r (ε a) (ε b)` and `l b < l a`, and `New.HCParam.lowerCount l r a` counts these `b`;
`New.Orbital.alternant ε κ` is the alternant over the permutations that preserve the signs `ε`;
`New.Orbital.torusEval x` evaluates a Laurent polynomial at a point `x` of the torus.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Orbital.oppositePairs`: The finite set of pairs of indices (a,b) with ε_a = +1 and ε_b = −1.
* `New.weylDimensionPoly`: The product of `λ i - λ j` over the pairs with `λ j < λ i`, divided by
  `∏_{i < card n} i!`, for `l = 2λ`.
* `New.HCParam.formalDegree`: For signs ε and l=2λ, the reciprocal of the integral over U(diag ε) of
  the squared modulus of the matrix coefficient `l.dsCoeff`, for the compact dual measure.
* `New.HCParam.kTypeChar`: `l.compactForm.lowestKType.kTypeChar` is the character of U(n) of
  highest weight λ − ρ.
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`, `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`: l=2λ has distinct entries ≡ n−1 mod 2, and
  |λ_i−λ_j| ≥ h whenever ε_i ≠ ε_j; `HasLargeGap A` is the gap h = 500n³+A.
modules.literature:
Known result: Discrete series character on the compact Cartan via orbital integrals, and formal
degree. This is done only for U(p,q), for parameters of gap 500n³+10n⁵ and for the explicit
coefficient of the lowest K-type. It gives the formal degree, and the stable sum of elliptic orbital
integrals as a multiple of the conjugate of Weyl's character of the compact form, both exact in the
compact dual measure. Source:
Harish-Chandra, Discrete series for semisimple Lie groups II: explicit determination of the
characters, Acta Math. 116 (1966), Thm 16 (with part I, Acta Math. 113 (1965), Thm 3); Knapp,
Representation Theory of Semisimple Groups (1986), Thm 12.7.

modules.title: Harish-Chandra parameters, c_λ, deg_λ, e_λ and holomorphic discrete series
modules.group: Flensted-Jensen's construction of discrete series
modules.note:
This file collects the definitions behind the discrete series of `G = New.USign ε`. A Harish-Chandra
parameter `λ` is stored as the integer vector `l = 2λ`, and the root `e_i - e_j` is positive when
`l j < l i`. The file proves elementary identities for `ρ`, `λ + ρ` and `Λ = λ + ρ - 2ρ_c`, and for
the gap condition. It then sets up Borel matrices, weights and holomorphic functions of weight `u`
for the holomorphic discrete series.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.HCParam.HasGap`, `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`: `λ` is regular, each `λ i` lies in
  `(n - 1) / 2 + ℤ`, and entries of `λ` with opposite signs `ε` are far apart, at least by the gap.
* `New.paramAddRho`, `New.HCParam.lowestKType`, `New.HCParam.casimirValue`, `New.weylDimensionPoly`:
  `λ + ρ`, `λ + ρ - 2ρ_c`, `|λ|² - |ρ|²` and the product of the positive roots at `λ` divided by
  `∏_{i < n} i!`.
* `New.weightMinors`, `New.HCParam.flenstedJensen`, `New.HCParam.dsCoeff`: a product of principal
  minors (`New.principalMinor`), Flensted-Jensen's integral of such products over `K`, and the
  function `c_λ` that it defines.
* `New.HCParam.formalDegree`, `New.HCParam.dsKernel`: `deg_λ = (∫ |c_λ|²)⁻¹` for the measure
  `New.haarU`, and `e_λ = deg_λ * conj c_λ`.
* `New.IsPosFirstOrder`, `New.IsKDominant`, `New.HasHolGap`: the indices of sign `1` come first; a
  weight does not increase within a block; a weight jumps up by at least `γ` from the first block to
  the second.
* `New.IsHolOfWeight`: a function on a product of copies of the group extends analytically to the
  products `h * b`, `b` invertible triangular, transforming under `b` by the character of weight
  `u`; an optional second sign vector restricts `h` and `b` to block diagonal matrices.

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign`: for a vector of signs `ε`, the unitary group `U(J)` of the diagonal matrix
  `J = New.signMatrix ε` with entries `ε i`.
* `New.principalMinor`: the determinant of the square submatrix on the indices with a given
  property.
* `New.haarU`: a measure on `U(J)` obtained from Lebesgue measure by a Cayley chart; a Haar measure
  for a hermitian involution `J`.
modules.literature:
The definitions are part of three known results, each treated in another file:
* Flensted-Jensen's function as the coefficient of the lowest K-type of a discrete series, in
  `Lib.DiscreteSeries.FlenstedJensen.PsiKTypes`;
* the lowest K-type and the Casimir value determine a discrete series coefficient, in
  `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Rigidity.HighestVectorsAndFiltration`;
* the highest coefficient of a holomorphic discrete series and its reproducing property, in
  `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Holomorphic.HighestVectorExtension`.

modules.title: Right derivatives and bump convolution for smooth functions on U(p,q)
modules.group: Flensted-Jensen's construction of discrete series
modules.note:
The file develops differential calculus on `U(p,q) = New.USign ε = U(diag ε)`. A smooth function on
the group is by definition the restriction of a smooth function on the matrix space, so no manifold
structure is needed. Continuous functions are convolved with compactly supported smooth functions
(bumps).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.smoothMatrixFunctions`, `New.SmoothU`: smooth `E`-valued functions on matrices, and their
  restrictions.
* `New.rightDerivMatrix`, `New.rightDeriv`: `gl_n(ℂ)` acts on them by right derivatives. An element
  `Y` of the real Lie algebra `New.unitaryLie J` acts by `f ↦ (x ↦ df_x(x Y))`, and the action
  extends `ℂ`-linearly through the splitting `X = Y₁ + i Y₂` of `New.eq_unitaryLiePart_add_I_smul`.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.Bumps`, `New.DiscreteSeries.bumpDeriv`: the smooth compactly supported
  functions, and the action on them of `gl n` by right derivatives.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.smear`: for continuous `F`, the linear map `α ↦ (g ↦ ∫ y, α y⁻¹ • F (g * y))`.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.hasDerivAt_smear`, `New.DiscreteSeries.rightDeriv_smear`: a right derivative
  of the convolution falls on `α`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign`: for a vector of signs `ε`, the unitary group `U J` of the diagonal matrix
  `J = diag ε`, which is `New.signMatrix ε`. For `g` in the group, `g.val.val` is its matrix.
* `New.unitaryLie`: the Lie algebra of `U J`, the real vector space of complex matrices `X` with
  `Xᴴ * J + J * X = 0`.
* `New.expU`: for `X` in `New.unitaryLie J`, the matrix exponential of `X` as an element of `U J`.
* `New.GlModule`: a `gl_n(ℂ)`-module structure on a complex vector space `M`, that is, a linear map
  from `n × n` matrices to endomorphisms of `M` that respects commutators.
modules.literature:
They are used for the function of Flensted-Jensen, the coefficient of the lowest K-type of a
discrete series (see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.FlenstedJensen.PsiKTypes`), and for two known results:
Schur orthogonality, and the fact that coefficients of integrable discrete series are cusp forms
(see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.CuspKernel`).

modules.title: Integrals of densities over unitary groups and over the flag variety of `K_ℂ`
modules.group: Flensted-Jensen's construction of discrete series
modules.note:
We study integrals over unitary groups `G = U(diag ε)` (`New.USign ε`) of functions that are
continuous on invertible matrices and transform under triangular matrices by the modulus character.
Here `New.IsBorelMatrix o b` says that `b` is invertible and upper triangular for the order `o`, `B`
denotes these triangular matrices, `New.diagChar (New.twoRho o _) b = ∏ i, b i i ^ (2ρ) i`, and `o`
is assumed injective. Integrals of such functions over `G` become integrals over an open part of
`U(n)`, and their integral over `U(n)` is invariant under left translation by invertible matrices.
As a consequence, a continuous function on the invertible block diagonal matrices `K_ℂ` that obeys
the same rule block by block has an integral over `K` that is invariant under `K_ℂ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.openOrbit`: the set `G B` of products of an element of `G` and a triangular matrix.
* `New.IsFlagDensity`: the transformation rule under triangular matrices.
* `New.integral_mul_left_eq_setIntegral_openOrbit`: the integral over `G` of a translate
  `F (x * g)` equals the integral over the part of `U(n)` in `x G B`.
* `New.integral_unitary_mul_left_of_density`: the integral over `U(n)` of such a function is
  invariant under left translation by an invertible matrix.
* `New.integral_haarK_mul_left_of_density`: the same for densities on `K_ℂ`, integrated over `K`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign ε`: the unitary group `U(J)` of the diagonal matrix of signs `J = New.signMatrix ε`.
* `New.twoRho l r`: the sum of the roots selected by `r` that are positive for `l`; its `i`-th entry
  is `#{j | r i j ∧ l j < l i} - #{j | r i j ∧ l i < l j}`.
* `New.lowerLiePart ε 1 o 2⁻¹`: the projection `X ↦ N - J Nᴴ J` to the Lie algebra of `U(J)`, where
  `N` is the part of `X` below the diagonal plus half its diagonal. `New.skewOfReal y` is the
  skew-Hermitian matrix with real coordinates `y`; `New.skewCoords` reads them back (real plus
  imaginary part over `√2` off the diagonal).
* `New.maxCompactU ε`, `New.haarK ε`: the group `K` of the elements of `U(J)` that commute with `J`,
  and its Haar measure of mass one.
modules.literature:
Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Character.FormalDegree` and
`Lib.DiscreteSeries.FlenstedJensen.PsiKTypes` for sources.

modules.title: Flensted-Jensen's integral, analyticity of c_λ and its Casimir eigenvalue
modules.group: Flensted-Jensen's construction of discrete series
modules.note:
This file studies the coefficient c_λ = `New.HCParam.dsCoeff l`, with `l = 2λ`, on the group
`U(diag ε)`, where `K = U(diag ε) ∩ U(n)`. It proves that c_λ is complex analytic, so defines a
smooth function `New.HCParam.dsCoeffSmooth` in `New.SmoothU`. For a parameter with a gap
(`New.HCParam.HasGap`, assumed in all results listed below), Flensted-Jensen's integral over `K`,
which gives c_λ, does not depend on the admissible block diagonal factor, and c_λ is an
eigenfunction of the Casimir operator of `gl_n`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.flenstedJensen_eq_of_accretive`, `New.dsCoeff_eq_flenstedJensen`: any block diagonal `a` with
  `a⁻¹ g` accretive (`Matrix.IsAccretive`: `z + zᴴ` positive definite) gives the same value. The
  integrand is a density on the flag variety of `K_ℂ`; polarization makes the integral locally
  constant, and the admissible `a` form a convex set.
* `New.flenstedJensen_eq_integral_of_eq_mul_mul_conjTranspose`,
  `New.dsCoeff_eq_integral_of_eq_mul_mul_conjTranspose`: the value as an integral over `K` for any
  splitting `g = p z qᴴ` with `p`, `q` block diagonal and `z` accretive.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.splitCoeff_triangular_mul_mul_triangular`,
  `New.DiscreteSeries.flenstedJensen_triangular_mul_mul_triangular`: block diagonal triangular
  factors, lower on the left and upper on the right, come out as characters.
* `New.casimir_dsCoeffSmooth`: the function c_λ (`New.HCParam.dsCoeffSmooth`, l = 2λ) on U(diag ε)
  is an eigenfunction of the Casimir operator Σ_{a,b} E_ab E_ba of gl_n, acting by right derivatives
  (`New.rightDeriv`), with eigenvalue `New.HCParam.casimirValue` l = |λ|² − |ρ|². Near a point c_λ
  is an average over k in K = `New.maxCompactU` of functions that are lowest weight vectors of
  weight λ + ρ (highest vectors for the roots positive for −l) in the basis k E_ab k⁻¹ of gl_n, and
  the Casimir operator does not depend on the basis.

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign`: For a vector of signs ε, the unitary group U(J) of the diagonal matrix J=diag(ε).
* `New.SmoothU`: Smooth functions on `U(diag ε)`: the restrictions of the smooth functions on all
  matrices.
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: the entries of `l = 2λ` are distinct, of the parity of `card n - 1`, and
  those with different signs differ by at least `2h`.
* `New.blockDiagAlg ε`: the matrices that commute with `diag ε`, the block diagonal matrices.

modules.title: First properties of c_λ and its K-types
modules.group: Flensted-Jensen's construction of discrete series
modules.note:
We study the function c_λ = `New.HCParam.dsCoeff` on U(diag ε). Here l = 2λ is a parameter, usually
assumed to satisfy `New.HCParam.HasGap`; K = `New.maxCompactU` has its Haar measure `New.haarK` of
mass one. We write m_w = `New.weightMinors` w for the product of principal minors that is the
coefficient of a highest vector for dominant w, and Λ = `New.HCParam.lowestKType` for the lowest
K-type; λ + ρ = `New.paramAddRho` l, with ρ half the sum of the roots positive for l. The first
properties of c_λ are read off from Flensted-Jensen's integral `New.HCParam.flenstedJensen` over K.
Then we compute ∫_K conj(m_ν(k)) c_λ(xkb) dk for a weight ν that is K-dominant for the order −l: it
is a constant times c_λ(x) c_λ(b) for ν = Λ, and 0 if ν − Λ is outside the cone
`New.HCParam.rootCone` of positive roots.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.dsCoeff_one`, `New.dsCoeff_of_mem_blockDiagAlg`, `New.dsCoeff_of_mem_maxCompactU`:
  c_λ(1) = 1, and c_λ = m_Λ on invertible block diagonal matrices, in particular on K.
* `New.dsCoeff_polar`: the formula for c_λ(p z q⁻¹) with p, q in K and z positive definite.
* `New.dsCoeff_inv`, `New.dsCoeff_neg`: inversion of g and λ ↦ −λ both conjugate c_λ(g).
* `New.integral_conj_weightMinors_lowestKType_mul_dsCoeff`,
  `New.integral_conj_weightMinors_mul_dsCoeff_eq_zero`: the projections of c_λ to its K-types.

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign`: for a vector of signs ε, the unitary group U(J) of the diagonal matrix J = diag(ε);
  `New.maxCompactU ε` is its compact subgroup K = U(diag ε) ∩ U(n).
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: the entries of `l = 2λ` are distinct and congruent to #n − 1 mod 2, and
  `|λ_i − λ_j| ≥ h` whenever `ε_i ≠ ε_j`.
* `New.IsKDominant`: the weight w is K-dominant for the order o if w_j ≤ w_i whenever ε_i = ε_j and
  o_i < o_j.
* `New.HCParam.rootCone`: the integer vectors β with o · β ≤ 0 for every vector o that strictly
  reverses the order of l: the polar cone of these vectors o.

Known result: Flensted-Jensen's function c_λ on U(p,q), classically the coefficient of the lowest
K-type of a discrete series, its first properties and its projections to K-types.

It is treated for U(p,q) and parameters with a gap, with the integrand written by principal minors;
existence of the discrete series is not assumed. Source: M. Flensted-Jensen, Discrete series for
semisimple symmetric spaces, Ann. of Math. 111 (1980) 253-311; B. Sun, Matrix coefficients of
cohomologically induced representations, Compositio Math. 143 (2007), Thm 1.1 (arXiv math/0403440);
A. Knapp, Representation Theory of Semisimple Groups (1986), ch. IX.

modules.title: Decay, tail bounds and the L² model of the discrete series coefficient c_λ
modules.group: Flensted-Jensen's construction of discrete series
modules.note:
Let `G = New.USign ε` be the unitary group of `diag ε`, let `l = 2λ` be a parameter, and let
`c_λ = New.HCParam.dsCoeff l` be its discrete series matrix coefficient. Norms of matrices are
operator norms on Euclidean space, and `a_g = New.blockDiagPart ε g` is the block diagonal part of
`g`. When `l` has gap `h`, Fischer's inequality gives `|c_λ(g)|² |det a_g|^h ≤ 1`, and the lower
bound `(‖g‖/2)² ≤ |det a_g|` turns this into polynomial decay of `c_λ`. The decay yields the
realisation of the module `U(𝔤)c_λ` in `L²(G)`. The file also gives explicit Lipschitz and tail
estimates for `l` with a big gap (`New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`) and entries bounded by `L`. Their
constants are polynomial in `L`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DiscreteSeries.norm_dsCoeff_le_pow`: if `l` has gap `h` (`New.HCParam.HasGap`) and `n` is
  nonempty, then |c_λ(g)| ≤ (2/‖g‖)^c for natural numbers c ≤ h.
* `New.HCParam.DsModule`, `New.HCParam.dsAction`, `New.HCParam.dsGenerator`: the module, its
  `gl n`-action by right derivatives, and its generator, which is `K`-highest by
  `New.isKHighest_dsGenerator`.
* `New.exists_smear_dsCoeffSmooth_eq`: every element of the module is an average
  ∫ α(y⁻¹) c_λ(g y) dy against a bump function α (a smearing of c_λ). This gives the decay bound
  `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap.exists_decay_bound`.
* `New.dsCoeff_schur_orthogonality`: Schur's product formula with the formal degree
  `New.HCParam.formalDegree`.
* `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap.toL2`: the embedding in `L²(G)`. The action is the derivative of right
  translation (`New.HCParam.HasLargeGap.isDerivedAction_toL2`), and each function is its own matrix
  coefficient against the generator
  (`New.HCParam.HasLargeGap.inner_toL2_dsGenerator_rightRegularL2`).
* `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap.isUnitaryCasimirGe`: the induced inner product is invariant, and the
  Casimir operator is at least `New.HCParam.casimirValue l`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest`: a vector x of a gl_n-module is K-highest of weight ν if each E_aa acts
  on it by ν_a and the compact raising operators kill it.
* `New.HCParam.dsCoeff`: the function c_λ(g) = Ξ(a, a⁻¹g) of a complex matrix g, with a the block
  diagonal part of g and Ξ the normalised integral `New.HCParam.flenstedJensen`.
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: the entries of `l = 2λ` are distinct and congruent to `n − 1` mod 2, and
  `|λ_i − λ_j| ≥ h` whenever `ε_i ≠ ε_j`.
* `New.HCParam.formalDegree`: for signs ε and l = 2λ, the reciprocal of the integral of |c_λ|² over
  U(diag ε) for the Haar measure normalised by the compact dual.

Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Rigidity.HighestVectorsAndFiltration`,

modules.title: Cayley chart and an explicit Haar measure on the unitary group U(J)
modules.group: Haar measure on unitary groups
modules.note:
For a hermitian involution J, this file builds an explicit Haar measure on the unitary group
`New.U J` through the Cayley chart and shows how it transforms. The Jacobians of the chart are
computed from the logarithmic derivative `Φᴴ J dΦ`, with real coordinates on skew-hermitian
matrices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.logDerivU`: the form `Φᴴ J dΦ` of a map `Φ` to `New.U J`; it is skew-hermitian
  (`New.conjTranspose_logDerivU`).
* `New.HasGaussianIntegral.measurePreserving`,
  `New.HasGaussianIntegral.exists_measurePreserving_equiv`: a linear isomorphism that matches the
  forms of two volumes normalised by `New.HasGaussianIntegral` preserves measure.
* `New.cayleyChart`: the chart y ↦ 2 (1 - X)⁻¹ - 1, X = J⁻¹ (`New.skewOfReal` y) / 2, which is
  (1 + X)(1 - X)⁻¹ where 1 - X is invertible; its density is `New.cayleyDensity`.
* `New.haarU`, `New.lintegral_eq_cayleyChart`: the measure, and integrals against it in the chart.
* `New.cayleyChart_jacobian`: the Jacobian of q ↦ a · cayleyChart J (y q) · b.
* `New.measurePreserving_haarU`: maps g ↦ a g b of unitary groups, for suitable a and b, preserve
  `New.haarU`. It follows that `New.haarU` is a Haar measure.

Notions from other files:

* `New.skewOfReal`, `New.skewCoords`: real coordinates on skew-hermitian matrices: the imaginary
  parts of the diagonal entries, and orthonormal coordinates of one entry in each pair off it.
* `New.HasGaussianIntegral a q`: the volume gives `exp (-t * q)` the integral `(π / t) ^ a` for
  all `t > 0`.
modules.literature: Part of a known result: the Haar measure of U(J) in Cayley coordinates.

modules.title: Coordinates for the Gram map
modules.group: Haar measure on unitary groups
modules.note:
Let `J` be a hermitian matrix. The Gram map sends a tuple of vectors, the columns of a complex
matrix `Y`, to the hermitian matrix `T = Yᴴ J Y`. Tuples carry Lebesgue measure `dY`, and hermitian
matrices the product `dT` of the Lebesgue measures of the entries on and above the diagonal.

* `New.joinCols`, `New.joinCol`: joining two groups of columns into one matrix; this preserves
  volume (`New.measurePreserving_joinCols`, `New.measurePreserving_joinCol`).
* `New.hermOfReal`, `New.gramCoords`: real coordinates on hermitian matrices, and the Gram map in
  these coordinates.
* `New.lintegral_eq_skewOfReal_add_hermOfReal`: Lebesgue measure on matrices `Z = S + T / 2` of size
  `n`, with `S` skew-hermitian and `T` hermitian, is `2 ^ (-n) dS dT`.
* `New.exists_measurePreserving_hermBlocks`, `New.exists_measurePreserving_hermCorner`: cutting a
  hermitian matrix into the corresponding blocks preserves volume.

Notions from other files:
* `New.skewOfReal`: the skew-hermitian matrix with given real coordinates, normalised so that
  Lebesgue measure in the coordinates is that of the entries on and above the diagonal.
* `New.skewCoords`: the real-linear left inverse of `New.skewOfReal`, inverse to it on
  skew-hermitian matrices.

modules.title: The polar formula for the Gram map on bases
modules.group: Haar measure on unitary groups
modules.note:
Let `J` be a hermitian involution of size `r` and `G = U(J)`, with the compact dual Haar measure
`dγ` (`New.haarU`). A basis `Y` whose Gram matrix `T = Yᴴ J Y` is near `J` is `γ σ(T)`, with `γ` in
`G` and `σ` a local section of the Gram map (`New.exists_isGramSection`).

* `New.IsGramSection.lintegral_eq`: the polar formula `dY = (vol U(r) / 2 ^ r) dγ dT`, where
  `vol U(r)` is `New.volU r`. The Jacobian is computed on tangent vectors: `Yᴴ J dY` has hermitian
  part `dT / 2`, and for fixed `T` it is `σᴴ (J γ⁻¹ dγ) σ`, which is skew-hermitian. The constant
  does not depend on the signature of `J`.

Notions from other files:
* `IsHermitianInvolution J`: the complex matrix `J` is hermitian and `J * J = 1`;
* `U J`: the group of `g` with `gᴴ * J * g = J`, where `volume` is the Haar measure `New.haarU J`,
  normalized so that it has mass `1` for `J = 1`;
* `gramCoords J Y`: the real coordinates of the hermitian matrix `Yᴴ * J * Y`;
* `cayleyChart J`: the Cayley parametrization of almost all of `U J` by real matrices `y` with
  `(cayleyDenom J y).det ≠ 0`; the density of the Haar measure there is `cayleyDensity J y` divided
  by `volU r`;
* `logDerivU (cayleyChart J) y`: the linear map `v ↦ γᴴ J dγ(v)`, with `γ = cayleyChart J y`;
* `skewAddHerm`: the linear equivalence from pairs of real matrices to complex matrices; its inverse
  sends `X` to the coordinates of the hermitian matrix `X + Xᴴ` and of the skew-hermitian matrix
  `(X - Xᴴ) / 2`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the invariant measure `dY / dT` on tuples of vectors with a given Gram matrix. Source:
C. L. Siegel, Über die analytische Theorie der quadratischen Formen, Ann. of Math. 36 (1935).

modules.title: Haar measure on U(J): U(n) has mass one, covering bounds for norm balls
modules.group: Haar measure on unitary groups
modules.note:
The measure `volume` on `U J` is the compact dual measure `New.haarU J`, normalised by
`New.volU n = ∏ i < n, 2 π ^ (i + 1) / i!`, the product of the areas of the unit spheres of
`ℂ, …, ℂ ^ n`. The first part shows that U(n) has mass one, by computing the image of Lebesgue
measure under the Gram map in two ways. For the second part let `J` be a hermitian involution of
size `n`, `j : S →* U J` a proper homomorphism, and `ν` a right invariant measure on `S` that is
finite on compact sets. Then norm balls are compared by a covering argument, with operator norms
throughout.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_hasGramDensity`: near the identity, the image of Lebesgue measure under the
  Gram map `Y ↦ Yᴴ Y` of square matrices is `volU n / 2 ^ n` times Lebesgue measure. One column
  ranges over a sphere, and the parts of the other columns orthogonal to it form a square matrix of
  size `n - 1`.
* `New.isProbabilityMeasure_haarU`: for `J = 1` the measure has mass one, by comparison with the
  polar formula `New.IsGramSection.lintegral_eq`. The same holds for the sign matrix with all signs
  equal to 1.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.measure_ball_le_covering`: for `D, R ≥ 1` the set `‖j s * y‖ ≤ R` has at most
  `(3 D R²) ^ (2 n²)` times the measure of the ball `‖j s - 1‖ ≤ 1 / D`.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.integral_decay_le`, `New.DiscreteSeries.lintegral_decay_le`: for `n ≥ 1` and a
  natural number `c > 8 n²` the function `(2 / ‖j s * y‖) ^ c` is integrable, with integral at most
  `16 ^ c` times the measure of `‖j s - 1‖ ≤ 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.gramCoords J Y`: the real coordinates `skewCoords (I • (Yᴴ J Y))` of the hermitian matrix
  `Yᴴ J Y`: with `x = I • (Yᴴ J Y)` they are `(x a b).re + (x a b).im`, divided by `√2` for `a ≠ b`.
* `New.U J`: the group of matrices `g` with `gᴴ J g = J`; thus `U 1` is the unitary group.
* `New.sphereDensity k r`: the number `2 π ^ k r ^ (k - 1) / (k - 1)!`.
modules.literature:
Known result: volume of U(n), polynomial volume growth of U(J).
Here J is any hermitian matrix with J² = 1, and the measure is normalised so that U(n) has mass one.
The covering bound for norm balls holds for any group with a right invariant measure and a
homomorphism to U(J), with an explicit crude constant. Source: L. K. Hua, Harmonic Analysis of
Functions of Several Complex Variables in the Classical Domains (1963), ch. III; I. G. Macdonald,
The volume of a compact Lie group, Invent. Math. 56 (1980); B. Gross, On the motive of a reductive
group, Invent. Math. 130 (1997).

modules.title: The fibre measure of the Gram map
modules.group: Haar measure on unitary groups
modules.note:
Let `J` be a hermitian involution of size `r` and `G = U(J)`. The Gram map sends a tuple of vectors,
the columns of a matrix `Y`, to the real coordinates (`New.gramCoords`) of the hermitian matrix
`T = Yᴴ J Y`.

* `New.LeGramFibre J E m`: the law of `g E` under the measure `m` on `G` is at most the fibre
  measure `dY / dT` on the tuples with the Gram matrix of `E`.
* `New.LeGramFibre.le_haar`, `New.leGramFibre_haar`: on the bases with Gram matrix `J`, which form
  the group `G`, the largest measure below the fibre measure is `vol U(r) / 2 ^ r` times the compact
  dual Haar measure `New.haarU J`, which is the `volume` of `U(J)`. Here `vol U(r)` is `New.volU r`.
* `New.LeGramFibre.append`, `New.LeGramFibre.append_vector`, `New.LeGramFibre.insert`: lower bounds
  for the fibre measure by choosing some vectors, moving them to a fixed position by an isometry,
  and choosing the others.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LeFibreMeasure μ ν π b l`: the measure `l` is at most the fibre measure of `μ / ν` for the
  map `π` over the point `b`.
* `New.gramCoords J Y`: the real coordinates of the hermitian matrix `Yᴴ J Y`; `New.hermOfReal t` is
  the hermitian matrix with coordinates `t`.
* `New.IsGramSection J V σ`: a differentiable section `σ` of the Gram map on the open set `V` of
  coordinates, with invertible values.
* `joinCols e (E₁, E₂)`, `joinCol e (E, v)`: the matrix with the columns of `E₁` and `E₂`, or of `E`
  and `v`, in the places given by `e`; `inclMatrix ℂ u` has the columns `e_{u k}`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the invariant measure `dY / dT` on tuples of vectors with a given Gram matrix. Source:
C. L. Siegel, Über die analytische Theorie der quadratischen Formen, Ann. of Math. 36 (1935).

modules.title: Maximal compact subgroup, block diagonal matrices and equivariance of minors
modules.group: Holomorphic discrete series and holomorphic forms
modules.note:
For signs `ε`, let `J = New.signMatrix ε`. `New.USign ε` is the unitary group of `J`,
`New.maxCompactU ε` is its subgroup of unitary matrices, `New.blockDiagAlg ε` is the algebra of
matrices that commute with `J`, and `New.blockDiagPart ε x` is the block diagonal part of `x`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.mem_blockDiagAlg`, `New.blockDiagPart_eq`: `New.blockDiagAlg ε` consists of the block
  diagonal matrices, and `New.blockDiagPart ε x` is `(x + J * x * J) / 2`.
* `New.mem_maxCompactU`: an element of the group is unitary exactly when it is block diagonal.
* `New.fderiv_eq_on_blockDiagAlg`: a complex derivative at `1` is determined on `New.blockDiagAlg ε`
  by the derivatives along one-parameter subgroups of `New.maxCompactU ε`.
* `New.IsKDominant.weightMinors_mul_borel`, `New.IsKDominant.weightMinors_oppBorel_mul`: let `o` be
  an injective order, `w` dominant within each block of `ε` (`New.IsKDominant`), `x` invertible and
  `b` invertible and block diagonal (`New.blockDiagAlg ε`). Multiplying `x` on the right by an upper
  triangular `b`, or on the left by a lower triangular `b`, multiplies `weightMinors w x` by
  `diagChar w b`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.weightMinors w g`: the coefficient of a highest vector of weight `w`, that is the product
  over all integers `t` of the principal minor of `g` on `{i | t ≤ w i}`, each factor with `t ≤ 0`
  divided by `det g`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Holomorphic.HighestVectorExtension` for sources.

modules.title: Exponentials in U(diag ε) and holomorphic extension of coefficients of highest vectors
modules.group: Holomorphic discrete series and holomorphic forms
modules.note:
The group is `New.USign ε = U(diag ε)` with compact subgroup `New.maxCompactU ε = U(diag ε) ∩ U(n)`.
Every element of the compact subgroup is an exponential, and every element of the group is a product
of two exponentials, so each element is joined to `1` by an analytic path in the group. A function
`F` on a product of copies of this group is holomorphic of weight `u` for the order `o`
(`New.IsHolOfWeight ε o u F ε'`) if it extends analytically to products `h * b` of tuples by
`F' (h * b) = (∏ τ, diagChar (u τ) (b τ)) * F h`. Here each `b τ` is triangular for `o`, and `h τ`,
`b τ` are block diagonal for `ε'` (no condition for `ε' = 1`). For injective `o`, products of
principal minors `New.weightMinors` of dominant weights (`weightMinors l g` is the product over
integers `t` of the principal minor of `g` on `{i | t ≤ l i}`, divided by `det g` when `t ≤ 0`) and
coefficients of highest vectors are such functions. For dominant weights the file computes their
weighted means over circles and, for a single copy of the group, their integrals against
`conj (weightMinors w)` over `New.maxCompactU ε`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_expU_eq_maxCompactU`: an element of the compact subgroup
  `New.maxCompactU ε = U(diag ε) ∩ U(n)` is the exponential of a block diagonal element of the Lie
  algebra (take the logarithm by the functional calculus).
* `New.exists_eq_expU_mul_expU`: every element of the group is a product of two exponentials, by the
  polar decomposition `New.exists_polar`.
* `New.isHolOfWeight_weightMinors`, `New.HCParam.IsKHighest.isHolOfWeight_coeffMap`: products of
  principal minors `New.weightMinors` and coefficients of highest vectors are holomorphic of a
  weight (`New.IsHolOfWeight`).
* `New.IsHolOfWeight.integral_mul_conj_weightMinors`: the integral of `F` against
  `conj (weightMinors w)` over the compact group `New.maxCompactU ε`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.unitaryLie J`, `New.expU`: the Lie algebra of U(J), made of the matrices `X` with
  `Xᴴ J + J X = 0`, and its exponential map to U(J).
* `New.blockDiagAlg ε`: the matrices that commute with `diag ε` (`New.signMatrix ε`), that is the
  block diagonal matrices for the signs `ε`.
* `New.IsBorelMatrix o b`: `b` is invertible and `b i j = 0` whenever `o j < o i`.
* `New.diagChar w b`: the product `∏ i, b i i ^ w i` of powers of the diagonal entries.
* `New.IsKDominant ε o w`: `w j ≤ w i` whenever `ε i = ε j` and `o i < o j`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the coefficient of the highest vector of a holomorphic discrete series representation
and its reproducing property. Here the setting is powers of U(p,q), using functions on the group
that extend holomorphically to the group times a Borel subgroup instead of the bounded domain.
Source: Harish-Chandra, Representations of semisimple Lie groups IV-VI, Amer. J. Math. 77 (1955), 78
(1956); A. Knapp (1986); A. Koranyi, A simplified approach to the holomorphic discrete series, arXiv
2312.16350.

modules.title: The holomorphic model function and discrete series coefficients in the holomorphic chamber
modules.group: Holomorphic discrete series and holomorphic forms
modules.note:
For signs `ε` on the indices and weights `u τ`, the model function `New.holMinorsPi ε u` is a
product over τ of quotients of products of principal minors `New.weightMinors` with weights
`u τ + c τ` and `c τ`. Here `c τ` is a large constant on the indices of sign `1` and zero elsewhere.
In the main results the order `o` puts the signs `1` first and each weight `u τ` is K-dominant for
it. With the indices numbered `1, …, n` along `o` and `u τ (n + 1) = 0`, each quotient is then the
product of the leading minors of size `i` to the powers `u τ i - u τ (i + 1)`, and the model
function is holomorphic of weight `u` (`New.IsHolOfWeight`). Let `w` be a K-dominant weight that
jumps up by at least `γ > 500 n³ + A + n + 1` from the first block to the second, where `n` stands
for the number of indices and `A` is a given natural number. Then the discrete series coefficient of
the parameter `2 w + 2 ρ` (`New.twoRho`) is the model function `New.holMinors ε w`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.isHolOfWeight_holMinorsPi`: `New.holMinorsPi ε u` is holomorphic of weight `u`.
* `New.IsHolOfWeight.circle_mean_holMinorsPi`: for `F` holomorphic of weight `u`, the mean over
  `|s| = 1` of `F (diag (s ^ o) * h)` divided by the character of weight `u` is
  `New.holMinorsPi ε u h * F 1`.
* `New.IsHolOfWeight.integral_mul_conj_holMinorsPi`: the reproducing formula
  `∫ F * conj m = (∫ |m|²) * F 1` for `m = New.holMinorsPi ε u`, if `F * conj m` is integrable.
* `New.IsHolOfWeight.eq_holMinorsPi_mul`: if `F g⁻¹ = conj (F g)`, then `F` is `F 1` times the model
  function.
* `New.dsCoeff_eq_holMinors`: for `w` as above, the parameter `2 w + 2 ρ` has gap `500 n³ + A`, and
  its coefficient `New.HCParam.dsCoeff` equals `New.holMinors ε w` on the unitary group. For the
  proof write a `g` near `1` as `x' * a * x` with `a` block diagonal and `x' - 1`, `x - 1` in the
  corner blocks; neither side sees `x'` and `x`, both agree at `a`, and both are analytic.

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign`: For a vector of signs ε, the unitary group U(J) of the diagonal matrix J = diag(ε).
* `New.IsHolOfWeight`: The function F on U(diag ε)^Φ extends analytically to products h b with b
  invertible and triangular for the order o, and the extension is the character of weight u at b
  times F(h). Optional signs ε' restrict h and b to block diagonal matrices; the default ε' = 1 is
  no restriction.
* `New.IsPosFirstOrder`, `New.IsKDominant`: The order o has distinct values and puts the signs +1
