modules.title: The peaks of a bounded holomorphic form lie away from the cusps
modules.group: Holomorphic discrete series and holomorphic forms
modules.note:
`(V.move g).firstMinimum` is the length of a shortest vector of the lattice at g, cut off at 1. It
is small deep in a cusp.

* `New.Rows.IsPeak`: a peak of a bounded function F is a point where |F| exceeds half of its
  supremum. At a peak x, |F| is at most 2|F(x)| everywhere and F(x) ≠ 0. A point where |F| is at
  least |F(x)| is again a peak.
* `New.Rows.exists_isPeak`: a bounded nonzero function has a peak.
* `New.Rows.IsPeak.le_firstMinimum`: let the order put the signs +1 first, and let F be a bounded
  form, holomorphic of a weight with gap 1 and entries in [-A, A] where A ≥ 2, and of a level
  p = -p̄ with im (Φ w p) in (0, A'] where A' ≥ 1. At every peak g of F the first minimum is at
  least (A A')^(-1/2).

A short lattice vector v is isotropic, and the transvection 1 - p v v^* J fixes F(g ·). Completing
squares writes the points n(z) = 1 - p z v v^* J of its one-parameter group, for im z > -1, as h b
with h real and b triangular (`New.Rows.exists_unitary_mul_triangular_of_pos`). The factor b^u is
bounded and tends to 0 as im z → ∞ (`New.Rows.exists_unitary_mul_triangular`). So z ↦ F(g n(z))
extends to a bounded holomorphic function of period 1 on im z > -1 that vanishes at i∞, and the
Schwarz lemma makes F(g) too small for a peak (`New.Rows.norm_le_of_transvection_invariant`). The
parameter is shifted by i, so that the half plane im z > -1 becomes the upper half plane and z = 0
becomes i.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsPosFirstOrder`: The order o has distinct values and puts every index of sign +1 before
  every index of sign −1.
* `New.Rows.IsAdelicHol`: For every adelic g, some φ is analytic at all products h b (h preserving
  diag(s), b invertible and triangular for o, at each infinite place) and φ(h b) = b^u F(g·(h,1))
  (`New.IsHolOfWeight`).
* `New.HasHolGap`: The condition on signs ε, integer vector w and natural number γ that
  w_i + γ ≤ w_j whenever ε_i = +1 and ε_j = −1.
* `New.Space`: A hermitian space with a point: a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx equal to
  diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places. `V.vecAtPoint y` is the adelic vector
  x⁻¹y, and `V.move g` is the space (J, xg).
* `New.Rows.rapidOfLevel`: The functions F that are continuous, left invariant under the rational
  points of V and right invariant under the principal level K(a), and that decay rapidly (members of
  `V.rapidFunctions`).
modules.literature:
Known result: Siegel's argument that a cusp form is large only away from the cusps. Here it is
proved for unitary groups over a CM field, for scalar functions of vector-valued weight and for
bounded forms, with half the supremum in place of an attained maximum. The distance from the cusp is
measured by the first minimum of the lattice, bounded below explicitly in weight and level. Source:
C. Poor, D. Yuen, Linear dependence among Siegel modular forms, Math. Ann. 318 (2000) 205-234, Thm
1.3; M. Eichler, Math. Ann. 213 (1975) 281-291; for the factorisation, Gill, Golub, Murray,
Saunders, Math. Comp. 28 (1974) 505-535.

modules.title: gl_n-modules, unitary representations of U(J) and a Casimir bound on K-highest vectors
modules.group: Rigidity of highest vectors in the discrete series
modules.note:
This file treats representations of the unitary group `New.U J` (the matrices g with gᴴJg = J) and
modules over `gl n` (`New.GlModule`), where `E_ab` acts by `New.GlModule.E`. Signs `ε : n → ℤˣ` fix
the compact subgroup `K`. They split `gl n` into 𝔨, spanned by the `E_ab` with `ε_a = ε_b`, and 𝔭,
spanned by the others. An integer vector `l` (a `New.HCParam ε`, read as 2λ) orders the indices, and
`E_ab` raises when `l_b < l_a`. For a symmetric relation r on the indices, `New.twoRho l r` is the
sum of the roots e_a − e_b with r(a, b) that are positive for this order. `New.GlModule.casimirK` is
the sum of `E_ab E_ba` over the pairs with `ε_a = ε_b`. For the constant sign it is the full Casimir
operator of `gl n`. κ_λ = |λ|² − |ρ|² is `New.HCParam.casimirValue l`, where ρ in this formula is
the half sum of the positive roots.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.GlModule`: a module over the Lie algebra of complex matrices; `New.GlModule.E` is the action
  of an elementary matrix, `New.GlModule.casimir` and `New.GlModule.casimirK` are Casimir operators.
* `New.IsUnitaryRep`: a representation on a normed space that is strongly continuous, of polynomial
  growth, and preserves a positive definite hermitian form.
* `New.IsDerivedAction`, `New.GlModule.IsCoeffMap`: the module is the derivative of a
  representation, or of a family of linear maps indexed by the group, along `New.expU` (the matrix
  exponential).
* `New.IsUnitaryCasimirGe`: the inner product is invariant, ⟨E_ab v, w⟩ = ε_a ε_b ⟨v, E_ba w⟩, and
  the full Casimir operator is bounded below by κ_λ.
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest.casimirK_eq_smul`: if `l.HasGap g`, the Casimir operator of 𝔨 acts on a
  K-highest vector by `New.HCParam.casimirKValue`.
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest.sum_card_sq_add_mul_nonneg`: if `l.HasGap g`, the inner product is
  invariant and the full Casimir operator is bounded below by κ_λ, a nonzero K-highest vector of
  weight Λ + ν gives Σ_a (n² + ν_a(ν_a + l_a)) ≥ 0, that is, |ν|² + 2⟨ν, λ⟩ ≥ −n³.
modules.literature:
Lowest K-type and Casimir value are known to determine a discrete series coefficient, via analytic
vectors. See `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Rigidity.HighestVectorsAndFiltration`.

modules.title: K-highest vectors, norm bounds, Casimir growth on the filtration, and analytic vectors
modules.group: Rigidity of highest vectors in the discrete series
modules.note:
The setting is a `gl_n`-module with an invariant inner product and a lower bound, depending on `l`,
for the Casimir operator (`New.IsUnitaryCasimirGe l ρ`). It is studied through the increasing
filtration `M_s = New.GlModule.filtration ρ ε x` generated by a `K`-highest vector `x`. Signs
`ε_a = ±1` define `𝔨`, spanned by the `E_ab` with `ε_a = ε_b`. `Ω_K = ρ.casimirK ε` is the Casimir
operator of `K`, and `c_K = New.HCParam.casimirKValue l` is its value on a highest vector. Take a
parameter with a large gap (`New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`) and `x` of weight `Λ`
(`New.HCParam.lowestKType`). Then the file shows that `Ω_K` grows along the filtration. With norm
bounds on the `M_s` it also shows that a bounded coefficient map is determined on `x` by its values
at `1` on the `M_s`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.HCParam.exists_highest_vector`: a nonzero finite-dimensional 𝔨-stable subspace contains a
  highest weight vector.
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest.finite_filtration`: for an invariant inner product, M_s has finite
  dimension.
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest.norm_apply_le_of_mem_filtration`: a matrix `X` maps `M_s` into `M_{s+1}`
  (`New.GlModule.apply_mem_filtration_succ`), with an explicit bound for the norm of this action
  (`New.HCParam.IsKHighest.norm_apply_le_mul_norm`).
* `New.mem_orthogonal_filtration_of_casimirK`: an eigenvector of `Ω_K` of eigenvalue at most
  `c_K(Λ) + s` that is orthogonal to `M_s` is orthogonal to every `M_t`.
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest.coeffMap_eq_zero`: let `l` be a parameter with a gap, and let `ρ` satisfy
  `New.IsUnitaryCasimirGe l ρ`. Then a bounded coefficient map that vanishes at `1` on the module
  generated by a `K`-highest vector `x` vanishes on `x` at every `g`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest`: x has weight ν and is killed by the compact raising operators.
* `New.GlModule.filtration`: M_0 = U(𝔨)x and M_{s+1} = M_s + Σ E_ab M_s.
* `New.HCParam.casimirKValue`: the integer |ν + ρ_c|² − |ρ_c|², the value of the Casimir operator of
  𝔨.
* `New.IsUnitaryCasimirGe`: the inner product of the gl_n-module H satisfies ⟨E_ab v, w⟩ = ε_aε_b⟨v,
  E_ba w⟩, and Re⟨y, Ωy⟩ ≥ κ_λ‖y‖² for the full Casimir operator Ω, with
  κ_λ = `New.HCParam.casimirValue l`.
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: the entries of l = 2λ are distinct, have the parity of n - 1, and those with
  different signs ε are at least twice the gap apart; `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap A` asks for a gap of
  at least `gapThreshold n A`, which puts such entries at least `1000 (card n)³` apart.
modules.literature:
Known result: Lowest K-type and Casimir value determine a discrete series coefficient, via analytic
vectors. Here the setting is U(p,q), and no irreducibility is assumed. Proved here are two parts: a
growth estimate for the compact Casimir operator along the filtration, for parameters with large
gaps, and a vanishing criterion for coefficient maps on a highest vector by explicit norm bounds in
place of analyticity.

Source: R. Parthasarathy, Classification of discrete series by minimal K-type, Represent. Theory 19
(2015) 167-185, Thm 1.1; earlier Hotta-Parthasarathy, Invent. Math. 26 (1974) 133-178; Schmid, Ann.
of Math. 102 (1975) 535-564; Vogan-Zuckerman, Compositio 53 (1984) Prop 6.1; Nelson, Analytic
vectors, Ann. of Math. 70 (1959) 572-615.

modules.title: The idempotent e_λ, the operator π(e_λ), and rigidity of highest vectors of type Λ
modules.group: Rigidity of highest vectors in the discrete series
modules.note:
The file studies the function `e_λ = New.HCParam.dsKernel l = deg_λ · conj c_λ` on `U(diag ε)`,
where `l = 2λ`, and the operator `π(f) = New.integratedRep π f = ∫ f(g) π(g) dg`. In the main
results `λ` has gap `500 n³ + A` (`New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`), `π` has growth `‖g‖ ^ A` and an
invariant positive definite sesquilinear form `B` on `X` (`New.IsUnitaryRep`), and the `gl n`-module
`ρ` on a complex space `M` is its derivative along a linear map `ι : M → X` (`New.IsDerivedAction`).

* `New.coeff_eq_dsCoeff_of_isKHighest` (rigidity): a `K`-highest vector `x` of weight
  `Λ = New.HCParam.lowestKType l` with Casimir value at least
  `κ_λ = New.HCParam.casimirValue l = |λ|² − |ρ|²` (ρ here the half-sum of positive roots) has the
  matrix coefficient `B x (π g x) = B x x c_λ(g)`.
* `New.integratedRep_fix_of_isKHighest`: if `‖g‖ ^ A f` is integrable and `f * e_λ = e_λ`, then
  `π(f)` fixes such a vector.
* `New.exists_integration_by_parts`, `New.integratedRep_dsKernel_casimir`: integration by parts, and
  `π(e_λ) Ω = κ_λ π(e_λ)`.
* `New.re_integratedRep_dsKernel_pos`, `New.integratedRep_eq_zero_of_notMem_rootCone`: a condition
  under which `π(e_λ)` does not kill a vector, and one under which it does.
* `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap.isIdempotentKernel_dsKernel`,
  `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap.exists_bump_conv_dsKernel`: `e_λ` is a minimal idempotent, reproduced by
  a bump function.

`ρ.casimirK 1` is the Casimir operator `Ω = ∑ E_ab E_ba` of all of `gl n` (all signs equal).

Notions from other files:
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest`: `x` is a `K`-highest vector of weight `ν`: each `E a a` acts on it by
  `ν a`, and it is killed by the compact raising operators, the `E a b` with `ε a = ε b` and
  `l b < l a`.
* `New.HCParam.lowestKType`: the integer vector Λ = λ+ρ−2ρ_c for a parameter l = 2λ, the highest
  weight of the lowest K-type.
* `New.HCParam.dsCoeff`, `New.HCParam.DsModule`: The function c_λ, and the module U(𝔤)c_λ it
  generates under right derivatives (action `New.HCParam.dsAction`, generator
  `New.HCParam.dsGenerator`).
* `New.weightMinors`, `New.HCParam.kTypeNormSq`: The coefficient m_ν of a highest vector of weight ν
  (a product of principal minors), and ∫_K |m_ν|².
* `New.HCParam.rootCone`: The cone of the positive roots for the order given by l.
modules.literature:
Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Rigidity.HighestVectorsAndFiltration`,
`Lib.DiscreteSeries.Theta.LocalCorrespondence` and `Lib.DiscreteSeries.FlenstedJensen.PsiKTypes` for
sources.

modules.title: Fock space oscillator actions, joint harmonics and Fischer decomposition
modules.group: Local theta correspondence for unitary dual pairs
modules.note:
This file treats polynomials in the variables of `T : New.FockDualPair`, indexed by rows `r : R` and
columns `c : C`. It defines the oscillator action `New.FockDualPair.oscRows` of `gl R` on the rows.
It also defines matched parameters and joint harmonics for the theta correspondence of
`U(ε) × U(ε')`, and proves that these notions are symmetric under `New.FockDualPair.swap`. A
Fischer-type analysis of orthogonal complements in bounded degree gives criteria for the Laplacians
to vanish.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.FockDualPair`, `New.FockDualPair.swap`: the data of the dual pair, and the data with
  `globalSign` negated and rows and columns exchanged.
* `New.FockDualPair.oscRows`: the action of `gl R` on the rows. The action of `gl C` on the columns
  is `oscRows` of `swap`, and its matrix units are given by `New.FockDualPair.swap_oscRows_E`.
* `New.FockDualPair.IsMatchedPair`, `New.IsMatch`: when the parameters `l = 2λ` and `l' = 2λ'`
  correspond.
* `New.FockDualPair.IsTermwiseHarmonic`, `New.IsJointHarmonic`: termwise harmonic polynomials, and
  joint harmonics that are highest for the lowest `K`-types `l.lowestKType` and `l'.lowestKType`.
  The signs `ε` and `ε'` are carried by the types of `l` and `l'`.
* `New.Fischer.fockLaplacian_eq_zero`, `New.Fischer.isLaplaceHarmonic_of_isKHighest`: criteria for
  the Laplacians `New.FockDualPair.fockLaplacian` to vanish.

Notions from other files:
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: `l.HasGap h` says that the entries of `l = 2λ` are distinct and congruent to
  `n − 1` mod 2, where `n` is their number, and `|λ_i − λ_j| ≥ h` whenever `ε_i ≠ ε_j`.
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest`: `x` is a `K`-highest vector of weight `ν`: each `E a a` acts on it by
  `ν a`, and it is killed by the compact raising operators, the `E a b` with `ε a = ε b` and
  `l b < l a`. The second condition alone is `New.GlModule.IsCompactPrimitive`.
* `New.HCParam.lowestKType`: for a parameter `l = 2λ`, the integer vector `λ + ρ − 2ρ_c`, which is
  the highest weight of the lowest `K`-type.
* `New.fockPairing`: the bilinear form `⟨P, Q⟩ = P(∂)Q(0)` on polynomials, for which monomials are
  orthogonal and `⟨x^d, x^d⟩ = d!`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Theta.LocalCorrespondence` for sources.

modules.title: The block rule for corresponding parameters
modules.group: Local theta correspondence for unitary dual pairs
modules.note:
The block rule compares two discrete series parameters at one place through their shifted entries.
This file proves that it is equivalent to matching for the oscillator pair, that it is kept by a
swap, a negation and a shift, and gives its form for a pair with one character. In the code all
entries are doubled, so that they are integers.

Notions from other files:
* `HCParam s`: an integer vector l = 2λ indexed by the domain of the signs s; `toHCParam s l` is l
  read as such a vector.
* `HasGap h`: the entries of l are distinct, of the parity of n − 1 for n entries, and those of
  opposite signs differ by at least 2h.
* `FockDualPair.std t s γ δ`: the oscillator pair with rows for the signs t, columns for the signs
  s, row shift γ and column shift δ + n' for n' rows (the constants added on the diagonal).
* `IsMatch`: both parameters have gap 500(n+n')³ and each row and each column is either matched,
  with a sign condition, or lies in the central range left by the difference of the ranks.
* `centredParam`: the entry of a row less twice the row shift, plus the number of columns; `swap`
  exchanges rows and columns.
* `IsMatchedPair`: the centred entries of a row and a column are opposite, and their signs times the
  centred row entry exceed the absolute difference of the ranks.
modules.literature:
Known result: the shape of the theta correspondence of discrete series parameters. Only statements
about the parameters, as integer vectors, are proved here. Sources: J.-S. Li, Theta lifting for
unitary representations with nonzero cohomology, Duke Math. J. 61 (1990); A. Paul, First occurrence
for the dual pairs (U(p,q), U(r,s)), Canad. J. Math. 51 (1999), 636–657.

modules.title: Weights of matched pairs and uniqueness of joint harmonics in Fock space
modules.group: Local theta correspondence for unitary dual pairs
modules.note:
This file studies the weights of matched pairs of the parameters `l` and `l'` of a dual pair
`T : New.FockDualPair`. It proves that the joint harmonic is unique up to a scalar, and that one of
its two weights suffices for this. Here `New.FockDualPair.IsMatchedPair` says that row `r` is
matched with column `c`.

The proof of uniqueness has three steps.
* The weights relative to the vacuum: `New.IsMatch.relWeight_eq_neg`,
  `New.IsMatch.sign_mul_relWeight_nonneg`.
* Both polarisations in a raising operator kill a highest harmonic polynomial, and a row has
  variables of one sign: `New.DiscreteSeries.polarisation_eq_zero_of_isCompactPrimitive`,
  `New.DiscreteSeries.polarisation_self_eq_smul_of_isCompactPrimitive`.
* Such a polynomial does not vanish at the 0-1 matrix of the matching:
  `New.IsMatch.eval_matchingPoint_ne_zero`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsMatch.unique`, `New.IsJointHarmonic.exists_eq_smul_of_row_weight`,
  `New.IsJointHarmonic.exists_eq_smul_of_column_weight`: the joint harmonic is unique up to a
  scalar, and one of its two weights suffices for this.
* `New.IsMatch.eval_matchingPoint_ne_zero`: a pre-joint harmonic does not vanish at the point
  `New.FockDualPair.matchingPoint`, the 0-1 matrix of the matching.

Notions from other files:
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: `l.HasGap h` says that the entries of `l = 2λ` are distinct and congruent to
  `n − 1` mod 2, where `n` is their number, and `|λ_i − λ_j| ≥ h` whenever `ε_i ≠ ε_j`.
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest`: `x` is a `K`-highest vector of weight `ν`: each `E a a` acts on it by
  `ν a`, and it is killed by the compact raising operators, the `E a b` with `ε a = ε b` and
  `l b < l a`. The second condition alone is `New.GlModule.IsCompactPrimitive`.
* `New.HCParam.lowestKType`: for a parameter `l = 2λ`, the integer vector `λ + ρ − 2ρ_c`, which is
  the highest weight of the lowest `K`-type.
* `New.FockDualPair.IsPreJointHarmonic`: `Φ ≠ 0` is killed by the compact raising operators of the
  columns and by the Laplacians of both sides, and is `K`-highest of weight `l.lowestKType` for
  rows.
* `New.FockDualPair.relWeight`: the entry in row `r` of the lowest `K`-type for `l`, minus the
  weight of the vacuum on a row of sign `ε r`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Theta.LocalCorrespondence` for sources.

modules.title: The Casimir elements of an oscillator pair
modules.group: Local theta correspondence for unitary dual pairs
modules.note:
An oscillator pair is given by a `FockDualPair` `T` with `n = card R` rows and `n' = card C`
columns; the first group acts on the rows. This file proves that, with the centres (the weights of
the twisting characters) removed, the Casimir elements of the two groups differ by the constant
`n n' (n - n') / 4`, and that for matching parameters the numbers `|u|² - |ρ|²` and `|u'|² - |ρ'|²`
differ by the same constant, where `u`, `u'` are the centred parameters, that is, the entries
shifted by the centres. By `HCParam.HasGap.casimirValue_sub_centre` these numbers are the centred
Casimir values.

The notions that the statements use:
* a parameter `l : HCParam ε` is an integer vector that stands for `l = 2λ`; `l.HasGap h` says that
  its entries are distinct, of the parity of `n - 1`, and at least `2h` apart where the signs `ε`
  differ;
* for symmetric `r`, `twoRho l r` is the sum of the roots selected by `r` that are positive for `l`,
  so `twoRho l ⊤` is `2ρ`, and `l.casimirValue` is `|λ|² - |ρ|²`;
* `T.oscRows` is the oscillator action of `gl R` on polynomials, and `T.swap` is the same pair with
  rows and columns exchanged;
* `T.centredParam l r` is `2u_r = l r - 2γ + n'` with `γ = T.rowShift` the scalar on the diagonal of
  the row action (`T.columnShift` is that of the column action `T.swap.oscRows`), and
  `IsMatch T l l'` says that `l` and `l'` have gap `500 (n + n')³`, that each row is matched with a
  column or has `|2u_r| < n - n'`, and that each column is matched with a row or has
  `|2u'_c| < n' - n`; the row `r` and the column `c` are matched if `u_r = -u'_c` and
  `T.globalSign * ε r * ε' c * 2u_r > |n - n'|`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the constant difference of the centred Casimir elements of the two groups of an
oscillator pair, a case of the correspondence of infinitesimal characters. Source: compare A. Paul,
First occurrence for the dual pairs (U(p,q), U(r,s)), Canad. J. Math. 51 (1999), Theorem 2.11.

See also `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Theta.LocalCorrespondence`.

modules.title: Existence of joint harmonics, Howe's argument and the local theta correspondence
modules.group: Local theta correspondence for unitary dual pairs
modules.note:
This file works in the polynomial (Fock) model of a dual pair of unitary groups. For matching
parameters, a joint harmonic is built as a product of minors along layers. For an oscillator pair,
the projection of a joint harmonic by the discrete series kernel is then nonzero, is fixed by
`π'(f)` for functions `f` that reproduce the kernel of the second group, and generates all projected
polynomial vectors under bump functions of the second group.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsLayering`: finitely many layers, each a list of rows paired with columns, of weight `ν`.
* `New.IsMatch.isLayering`: for matching parameters (`New.IsMatch`) the sets of variables
  `New.FockDualPair.Layer` are layers of weight `New.HCParam.lowestKType l`.
* `New.IsMatch.exists_isJointHarmonic`: hence a joint harmonic (`New.IsJointHarmonic`) exists.
* `New.IsJointHarmonic.howe_argument`: in the polynomial (Fock) model with its row action
  `T.oscRows` and column action `T.swap.oscRows`, a subspace that is stable under the columns,
  contains a joint harmonic (`New.IsJointHarmonic`) and contains certain images of the row operators
  is the whole space.
* `New.OscillatorPair.re_inner_integratedRep_pos`: for a joint harmonic `Φ` and `Φ₁ = π(e_λ) Φ`,
  with `e_λ` the discrete series kernel, `⟨Φ, Φ₁⟩` has positive real part.
* `New.OscillatorPair.integratedRep_integratedRep_eq_self`: `π'(f) Φ₁ = Φ₁` for every `f` of
  suitable decay that reproduces `e_λ'`; the proof compares the Casimir operators of the two groups
  on `Φ` and uses `New.integratedRep_fix_of_isKHighest`.
* `New.OscillatorPair.exists_bump_integratedRep_eq`: every `π(e_λ) P` is obtained from `Φ₁` by a
  bump function of the second group; the proof rests on `New.IsJointHarmonic.howe_argument`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.HCParam.IsKHighest`: each matrix unit `E a a` acts on `x` by `ν a`, and `x` is killed by the
  compact raising operators, the `E a b` with `ε a = ε b` and `l b < l a`.
* `New.IsJointHarmonic`: `l` and `l'` match (`New.IsMatch`), and `Φ ≠ 0` is highest for rows and
  columns, of the weights of the two lowest `K`-types, and harmonic along rows and columns.
* `New.OscillatorPair`: two commuting oscillator representations on one Fock space, one acting on

Known result: Theta correspondence of discrete series for real unitary dual pairs, with joint
harmonics. Only matched parameters with large gaps on Fock space are treated. The joint harmonic
exists and is unique up to scalar, and its projection is fixed by the partner's `π'(f)` for every
`f` of suitable decay that reproduces the partner's discrete series kernel. The projection of every
polynomial vector is a compactly supported smoothing, under the second group, of the projected joint
harmonic. Source: J.-S. Li, Theta lifting for unitary representations with nonzero cohomology, Duke
Math. J. 61 (1990) 913-937; R. Howe, Transcending classical invariant theory, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2
(1989); A. Paul, First occurrence for the dual pairs (U(p,q), U(r,s)), Canad. J. Math. 51 (1999)
636-657, Theorem 2.7.
